heading: 6 Essential Responsibilities the Movement Expects from Citizens
subheading: A constitution is only as strong as the citizens willingness to live by its principles and defend its safeguards in everyday public life.
progressText: You have committed to {{count}} of 6 Citizen Duties

items.title: LEARN
items.description: Read the Constitution and understand the Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties. Know what the Constitution guarantees and what it expects from each of us. Be aware of the threats to constitutional values, democratic institutions, fundamental rights and the rule of law, and recognise when and where they are being undermined.
items.commitment: I will read, discuss and deepen my understanding of the Constitution, and remain alert to threats to its values and safeguards.

items.title: PARTICIPATE
items.description: Democracy is not limited to voting once in five years. It is a continuous relationship between citizens and public institutions. Stay informed about public affairs, vote thoughtfully, engage with elected representatives and public authorities, participate in Gram Sabhas, ward meetings and public consultations, and raise issues affecting your community.
items.commitment: I will not be a passive spectator of democracy. I will stay informed, vote responsibly, participate in public life, question those in power respectfully, raise issues that affect my community, and contribute peacefully to finding solutions.

items.title: VOLUNTEER
items.description: Treat every person with equality, dignity and compassion, regardless of religion, caste, gender, language, disability, social background or any other difference. Do not ignore when individuals or communities face discrimination, violence, exclusion or injustice. Stand in solidarity with those who are vulnerable or victimised, and help them access justice and protection.
items.commitment: I will stand with those who face injustice, discrimination or vulnerability. I will not remain a silent bystander; I will offer support, speak up peacefully, and help those in need seek justice and dignity.

items.title: DISCERN
items.description: In an age of misinformation, manipulation and polarising social media, responsible citizenship requires us to think critically and seek reliable information before forming or spreading opinions. Reject rumours, hatred and unverified allegations. Encourage reason, scientific temper, open-mindedness and respectful disagreement.
items.commitment: I will think before I share, question before I believe, and disagree without spreading hatred or dehumanising others.

items.title: DEFEND
items.description: When constitutional rights, democratic freedoms, the rule of law or the independence of public institutions are threatened, every one of us has the responsibility to respond. Question the misuse of public power, demand transparency and accountability, document violations responsibly, and use peaceful, lawful and constitutional means to seek remedies.
items.commitment: I will speak up when constitutional values and democratic freedoms are threatened, hold power accountable through lawful means, and stand up for the Constitution and the rule of law.

items.title: UNITE
items.description: Constitutional democracy is a shared responsibility. Let us come together across our differences and build a broad, peaceful and inclusive movement rooted in constitutional values. Build bridges, not walls. Reach out to others, listen to different voices, and bring more people into this democratic effort.
items.commitment: I will reach out to others, bring more people into this movement and work together peacefully to strengthen constitutional democracy.
